Class GameState

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.model.gamemanager.GameState
public class GameState extends Object
Holds and manages all mutable game data for a single match.

This class is the central data store accessed by GameManager and the phase state machine. It owns the card lists (deck, buildings, upper and lower display rows), the board and queue tiles, the player list, the current player, turn/age counters, and the pending action queue. It also exposes the operations that mutate this data in response to player actions and phase transitions.

  • Field Details

    • MIN_PLAYERS

      public static final int MIN_PLAYERS
      The minimum number of players supported by a match.

      This lower bound is enforced by GameState(List, int) and mirrors the range of player counts that GameInitializer is able to set up (decks, boards, queues, and display rows are only defined for 2–5 players).

  • Constructor Details

    • GameState

      public GameState(List<Player> players, int numPlayers)
      Constructs a GameState with the given player list and player count, initializing all collections to empty and counters to their starting values. Call initialize() to populate the game data before play begins.
      Parameters:
      players - the list of players participating in the match
      numPlayers - the total number of players
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if numPlayers is not between 2 and 5 (inclusive)

    • GameState

      public GameState(GameSnapshot snapshot, List<Player> players)
      Reconstructs a GameState from a previously saved GameSnapshot, restoring every piece of mutable game data (decks, display rows, board, queue, age/turn counters, pending actions, and the current player) exactly as it was at the time of the snapshot.

      Unlike GameState(List, int), numPlayers is not re-validated against MIN_PLAYERS/MAX_PLAYERS here: the snapshot is assumed to originate from a match that was already validated when it was first created.

      Tile-to-player object references broken by JSON deserialization are intentionally left unrestored here; callers are responsible for invoking the appropriate reconnection logic after construction (see RestoredGameManager).

      Parameters:
      snapshot - the snapshot to restore the state from
      players - the players participating in the restored match

    • initialize

      public void initialize()
      Initializes all game data for a new match.

      Loads and shuffles the deck, building deck, board, queue, and display rows via GameInitializer. Players are shuffled and assigned to queue tiles in random order. The first player in the shuffled order becomes the starting current player. Initial food is distributed according to turn order.

    • assignInitialFood

      private void assignInitialFood()
      Assigns starting food to each player based on their position in the turn order. Earlier players receive less food to compensate for the first-mover advantage.

    • advanceAge

      public void advanceAge()
      Advances the match to the next age.

      Increments the age counter (up to 3), removes building cards from the lower row when entering age 3, moves any remaining building cards from the upper row to the lower row, and adds the new age's building cards to the upper row.

    • applyNextPlayer

      public void applyNextPlayer(GamePhaseEnum currPhaseState)
      Advances the current player to the next one in turn order.

      During the setup phase, or when no player is on the board, the next player is taken from the front of the queue. In all other phases, the next player is the first one currently occupying a board tile.

      Parameters:
      currPhaseState - the current game phase, used to determine the selection strategy

    • applyEvents

      public EventDTO applyEvents(GamePhaseEnum phase)
      Applies all event cards in the display row appropriate for the given phase, collecting the results into an EventDTO.

      During GamePhaseEnum.END_ROUND, event cards are read from the lower row; during GamePhaseEnum.PLAY_EVENT, from the upper row. After events are applied, updated player stats are added to the DTO.

      Parameters:
      phase - the game phase determining which display row to process
      Returns:
      a DTO summarising all event effects and updated player stats

    • applyDraw

      public void applyDraw(Card card, GamePhaseEnum phase) throws InvalidDrawException
      Resolves a draw action by the current player for the given card.

      The draw type (upper or lower) is inferred from which display row the card belongs to. A matching pending action must exist, and the card must pass validation by DrawCardVisitor; otherwise an InvalidDrawException is thrown. On success, the action is removed from the queue, the card is removed from its row, and its instant and interactive effects are applied.

      Parameters:
      card - the card the player wants to draw
      phase - the current game phase, passed to instant effect resolution
      Throws:
      InvalidDrawException - if no matching pending draw action exists or the card fails validation

    • toSnapshot

      public GameSnapshot toSnapshot(int matchId, GamePhaseEnum phase)
      Serializes the current game state into a GameSnapshot for persistence.

      All mutable collections are copied into new lists to avoid aliasing. Pending actions are converted to GameSnapshot.PendingAction records; actions without an owner are recorded with the placeholder nickname "SYSTEM".

      Parameters:
      matchId - the unique identifier of the match being snapshotted
      phase - the current game phase at the time of the snapshot
      Returns:
      a GameSnapshot representing the full current state
